positions.stance: Wants to reduce electric bills by expanding the grid using already-cleared spaces and exploring new wind and solar methods that use existing infrastructure.
Would stop private corporations from buying up homes, build transitional and citizen-owned price-stabilized housing, and "make it illegal to take someone's house for delinquent property taxes."
Would target "unfair market manipulation of middlemen in the food supply chain" and reprioritize crop subsidies toward lowering prices of healthy foods.
Proposes no income taxes on earnings under $40k a year, bans on bank junk fees, right-to-repair laws, and universal paid family leave.
Supports "Medicare/ Gov. quality HealthCare for all," getting rid of insurance companies, letting Medicare negotiate, and capping life-saving drugs at $5-$10.

H6NJ03192.name: Ryan Michael Kelly
H6NJ03192.bio: Former Lake Como Borough Council member and college instructor who spent nearly 13 years in the DHS Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties.

positions.stance: Focus on policies that lower everyday costs through "competition, transparency, and enforcement where markets are failing people," plus targeted tax relief for working families and small businesses.
Supports the right to organize and bargain collectively, opposes so-called Right to Work laws, and backs a living wage, paid parental leave, and PRO Act-style protections.
"I support universal, single-payer healthcare," treating healthcare as a public good not dependent on employer, income, or age.
Calls for substantially more affordable housing including public and social housing, broadly applicable rent stabilization, and Housing First approaches to homelessness.
Supports more VA healthcare and claims staff, shorter disability claims delays, expanded mental health care, and better outside-care access when the VA cannot provide timely treatment.

H4NJ03247.name: Steven Welzer
H4NJ03247.bio: Former college-level economics instructor, writer, and a founder of the Green Party of New Jersey.

positions.stance: Running because establishment-party policies are leading to crisis; says it is time to open up the political system to "more voices and more choices."
Bases his platform on the national Green Party's: "Ecological Responsibility, Social Justice, Grassroots Democracy, and Peace (anti-militarism)."

H6NJ05247.name: Adam Rueda
H6NJ05247.bio: Bucknell graduate who has worked as a senior financial analyst at a commercial real estate brokerage, an interior design salesperson, and a DJ.

positions.stance: Pledges "to never own stocks or crypto while serving in office" and to work to end insider trading and limit corporate and international influence on Congress.
Prioritizes addressing human rights violations in Gaza, the West Bank and greater Palestine, and due-process violations by ICE, especially in detention centers.
Says "we must work to restore free speech online, in the workplace and in the media," citing social media censorship and coercive workplaces.

wiki:aristotle-eliopoulos.name: Aristotle Eliopoulos
wiki:aristotle-eliopoulos.bio: Teacher and union representative raised in Jersey City.

positions.stance: Would increase federal support for public schools, restore classroom discipline, expand career and technical education, and reduce unnecessary standardized testing.
Supports expanded early intervention, more special education funding, better access to therapies, and stronger protections under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act.
Would cut taxes for working and middle-class families, expand the Child Tax Credit, reduce healthcare and drug costs, and eliminate wasteful government spending.
Encourages workforce and affordable housing construction, first-time homebuyer incentives, and protection of seniors from being priced out, and would crack down on predatory corporate speculation.
Supports union workers and collective bargaining, apprenticeships and skilled trades, bringing manufacturing jobs back to America, and infrastructure investment.

H6NJ08217.name: Da’Shone Hughey
H6NJ08217.bio: Entrepreneur, educator, author, and technology innovator focused on AI, robotics, workforce training, and education reform.

positions.stance: Expanding access to technology education, digital literacy, robotics, and AI learning "so young people are ready to compete and lead."
Building direct pathways from education to employment in fields like robotics, HVAC, data infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, and technology services.
Supporting entrepreneurs with access to capital, technical assistance, and public-private partnerships that help them grow and hire.
Fighting for policies that create opportunity in underserved neighborhoods and strengthen the middle class.
Investing in future-focused industries and training systems to make communities stronger and more resilient.
"Resist fascism. End abortion." Says "Abortion is genocide" and that showing the victims of abortion to Americans is essential to a more progressive tomorrow.
Would protect current retirees, strengthen Social Security's long-term finances, and preserve it for future generations.
Calls for practical solutions to the underlying costs of housing, energy, healthcare, food, taxes, and necessities while expanding good-paying jobs.
Would make care systems easier to navigate, expand respite and home-care options, and protect caregivers' ability to stay in the workforce.
Calls for stronger fraud prevention, better consumer education, modern law enforcement tools, and accountability for institutions protecting money and personal information.
Wants transparency on costs and outcomes, more affordable paths to degrees and credentials, and stronger apprenticeships and technical education.

H6NJ12441.name: Andres Jinete
H6NJ12441.bio: Union member and community organizer who worked for many years at a community library.

positions.stance: Supports a renter's "bill of rights," major public housing investment toward social housing, and a Housing First approach to homelessness.
"Free single-payer universal healthcare available to everyone, regardless of status."
Would "purchase and forgive all student debt" and expand tuition-free state and community colleges and free vocational training.
Would raise the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour indexed to inflation and institute a 32-hour workweek without reduced pay.
Calls to abolish ICE, dismantle DHS, and overhaul the immigration system including a new amnesty and closing detention centers.
Runs a self-funded "zero-donor campaign," accepting no money from anyone, and would champion H.R. 415, the Stop Act, banning congressional call-time fundraising.
Proposes an Employer of Last Resort program: a "federal job guarantee with a $50,000 minimum salary."
Supports a Universal Livable Income providing a "livable floor above poverty" that complements the job guarantee.
Proposes a wealth cap and automation dividend to redistribute wealth from automation and monopolies.
Would reinvest automation gains into human labor and retraining.

H6VA02263.name: Matt Baker
H6VA02263.bio: Retired U.S. Marine Corps colonel (28 years) who has spent a decade modernizing power systems for the DoD and utilities.

positions.stance: "January 6th is my litmus test"; says organized individuals attacked the Capitol and "Democracy is non-negotiable."
Says adding trillions to the debt while claiming fiscal conservatism is a performance: "I will not perform fiscal conservatism. I will practice it."
"A woman has a right to choose. This is settled for me."
"The Second Amendment is the law of the land. Common-sense regulation is also the law of the land. Both are true simultaneously."
"Reagan compromised. So should we"; supports a workable solution combining a pathway, enforcement, and human dignity.

H6VA02248.name: Makiba Gaines
H6VA02248.bio: Practicing civil rights attorney in solo practice.

positions.stance: Says working people and small businesses are buried under taxes, tolls, and government fees, and that "it is time to put Americans first."
Intends to reduce government corruption, fraud, and waste and redirect those funds to programs Americans rely on.
Would increase funding to community programs and to home-ownership and entrepreneurship programs to reduce poverty and crime, working with law enforcement.
Says "Social media has to be regulated"; supports Congress limiting media monopolies and giving Americans more control over their accounts.
Calls for increasing Social Security benefits for seniors and disabled Americans and properly funding Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security.

H6VA03139.name: Steve Woll
H6VA03139.bio: Navy veteran, scientist, and businessman who has applied science and technology to problems for the Navy and private industry.

positions.stance: Would end partisan gerrymandering through independent citizen commissions and reverse Citizens United: "elections should not be an auction."
Would restore a politically independent Department of Justice and have Congress reassert itself as a co-equal branch.
Would ban congressional and executive stock trading and political betting markets and bar lobbying for 10 years after leaving Congress.
"Balance the budget"; would fix entitlements honestly and enforce "No Congressional budget, no Congressional pay."
Says backing away from alliances and a rules-based international order has made America less safe and less respected, and recovery must start now.
Urges voters to "Vote NO on Virginia's Amendment 1" and "Say No to late term abortion in Virginia," saying "To end abortion, we too must show the victims."
Proposes career-linked digital training, entrepreneur centers, and a rapid-response pathway for career changers and federal workers in transition.
Says service should lead to civilian prosperity; supports veteran startup mentoring, responsible financing, and remote-work opportunities for military families.
Supports career pathways, trauma-informed mentorship, and housing-bridge pathways so no one must remain in danger for lack of a job or safe home.
Supports multilingual learning, digital-certification pathways, and immigrant-owned startups, calling immigrant communities "a source of skill, language, entrepreneurship, and leadership."
Supports factory-built, energy-smart housing, ADU options, and ownership structures that help working families build equity.

wiki:taner-lopez.name: Taner Lopez
wiki:taner-lopez.bio: Former university instructor who later served as a cultural advisor supporting the Department of Defense.

positions.stance: Drafted the American Controlled Immigration, Workforce and Security Act to restore border control and create a vetted process for undocumented immigrants to work legally.
His Data Center Community Consent Act would give affected property owners information and a consent vote before massive data center projects.
His American Working Farms Act would help family farms stay working farms across generations and reduce the after-tax cost of lawful farm labor.
His Veterans 28 Act would give veterans community care if the VA cannot provide an appointment within 28 days.
His Human Existential Protection Act would bar autonomous AI control of weapons of mass destruction and require human-controlled emergency shutdown capabilities.

H6VA07312.name: Randall Terry
H6VA07312.bio: Founder of Operation Rescue and 2024 Constitution Party candidate for president.

positions.stance: Runs TV ads urging "Vote no amendment one" and "Say No to late term abortion in Virginia," saying "To end abortion, we too must show the victims."

wiki:shelly-arnoldi.name: Shelly Arnoldi
wiki:shelly-arnoldi.bio: U.S. Navy veteran and licensed Professional Engineer with 27 years managing facilities and construction projects for the military and cultural institutions.

positions.stance: Would put parents back at the center of education, defend parental rights, and have schools return to teaching the fundamentals.
Would cut taxes and red tape on small businesses and hold data centers responsible for their own energy and water.
Supports term limits, transparent budgets, and ending special-interest influence; has signed the U.S. Term Limits pledge.
"Stand with our first responders. Enforce the laws on the books."

H6VA08336.name: Tim Sharman
H6VA08336.bio: Customer-experience professional and founder of the startup trulyus.app.

positions.stance: Will make affordability a daily priority, attacking underlying costs of housing, childcare, healthcare, and education through efficiency, smarter regulation, and higher wages.
Wants to reopen paths to homeownership, education, good jobs, and entrepreneurship: "Prosperity isn't the problem. Prosperity becoming a closed club is."
Would introduce the American Opportunity Fund Act, chartering a privately funded nonprofit for voluntary, public contributions to expand opportunity.
"I will never vote to shut down the federal government"; supports reforms to end shutdowns as a political weapon.
Says local communities should decide whether data centers are built and that data centers should pay the infrastructure costs they create.
"I am pro-choice in the first trimester and pro-life in the last trimester" with an exception when the mother's life is at risk.
"I fully support all local legislative efforts to completely ban new data center construction" and federal legislation to manage their negative externalities.
Supports a bipartisan climate bill that aggressively expands clean and renewable energy, invests in mineral supply chains and manufacturing, and includes real permitting reform.
Supports enforcement and a secure border, opposes "ICE thuggery," and supports permanent residency for undocumented immigrants without a path to citizenship.
"I will fight hard for a balanced budget as that is the key to reducing inflation long term."

H4VA10154.name: Dianne Blais
H4VA10154.bio: Peace activist and volunteer who convenes the Jane Addams branch of the Women's International League for Peace and Freedom US.

positions.stance: Says wars and war preparation have huge costs and environmental impacts; wants tax money spent at home rather than "trying to bend countries to our will."
Adopts Ralph Nader's Compact for America, including a $15 minimum wage, higher taxes on the wealthy and corporations, and Medicare for all.
Adopts RootsAction Education Fund's Foreign Policy Primer for U.S. Congressional Candidates as her international platform.
Wants "a moratorium of data centers, free public transit, open borders, improved incarceration, and a basic return to pre-2025 status quo."
Would like ranked choice voting and proportional representation.

H6AZ01488.name: Monica Alponte
H6AZ01488.bio: Retired business owner, writer, and former political TV talk show co-host.

positions.stance: "No more sending American taxpayer dollars into endless foreign wars"; calls for putting Americans' needs first.
"Abolish the IRS, end the Federal Reserve's monopoly on our currency, and return the stolen trillions directly to the American family."
Supports keeping the border secure and ending incentives for illegal immigration.
Would "unleash free markets and voluntary trade without government interference."
Would protect individual liberty, letting each person live as they choose so long as they don't harm others, and limit government to protecting constitutional rights.

H4AZ03174.name: Alan Aversa
H4AZ03174.bio: Physics and computer programming teacher, currently a substitute teacher for charter schools.

positions.stance: Says abortion has "unjustly taken the right to life away from millions of innocent persons" and seeks to protect the right to life for all.
Believes parents are children's first educators with a right to choose how to educate them; opposes promoting transgender and CRT ideologies in schools.
"We must return to the land"; says local sustainable farming solves unemployment and capital must be equitably distributed and decentralized.
Opposes U.S. involvement in and funding of wars by Israel, Ukraine, Iran and elsewhere; says "America first."
